questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between Tableau Next and Tableau Desktop/Cloud?
options: Tableau Next is the next version number of Tableau Desktop
Tableau Next replaced Tableau Desktop, which no longer exists
Tableau Next is a separate, Salesforce-native product; Tableau Desktop and Cloud continue to exist
They are the same product sold under two names
questions.explain: Tableau Next is a separate offering built on the Salesforce platform. The traditional Tableau products continue.

questions.q: What serves as the data foundation for Tableau Next?
options: Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud)
Only local Excel files on a laptop
A Tableau Server repository
SOQL queries run at view time
questions.explain: Data 360 is the data layer; Tableau Next reads its data model objects, data lake objects, and calculated insight objects.

questions.q: What is Tableau Semantics used for?
options: Compressing CSV files
Sending email alerts to customers
Managing user passwords
Adding business meaning, such as relationships and metric definitions, in a semantic model
questions.explain: Tableau Semantics is the semantic layer that organizes data and defines its business meaning for people and AI.

questions.q: In Tableau Next, what is a workspace?
options: A structured place to create and reference analytics assets like data, semantic models, vizzes, and dashboards
A physical office desk assigned to an analyst
A single chart
A Data 360 identity resolution ruleset
questions.explain: Workspaces organize a team's analytics assets, which may also be referenced from other workspaces.

questions.q: What key difference from a Tableau Desktop workbook does this lesson highlight?
options: Tableau Next cannot make charts
Data, semantics, visualizations, and dashboards are separate assets, so definitions live in a shared semantic model
Tableau Next requires installing a desktop application
A workbook in Tableau Next cannot contain a filter
questions.explain: A Desktop workbook bundles connection, calculations, and views. Tableau Next separates them so one governed semantic model can serve many visualizations.
